candidates.computation_change_reason: The table defines multiple numeric columns (Ca, Ce, acute/chronic aquatic, domestic supply, human health, irrigation, wildlife, livestock, and TMDL-related columns); different readings of which column supplies the enforceable limit change the applicable discharge limit and exceedance outcome.

Method quantitation limits govern whether reported measurements support a numeric compliance comparison or should be treated as below-quantitation/no ordinary numeric result, affecting limit exceedance evaluation and missing-evidence classification.

The effluent Ce cell is blank while other criteria columns contain values; interpretation of whether no numeric effluent limit applies versus whether a limit exists elsewhere in the row affects enforceable-limit selection and whether absent measurements are non-comparable or unresolved.

Ce is populated (5.04 ug/l) alongside multiple other numeric criteria in the same row; choosing Ce versus another column as the operative limit changes the enforceable discharge limit and exceedance determination for total mercury.

The parenthetical (P) may denote a priority or permit-specific parameter designation; different readings change whether this pollutant form is subject to enforceable limits and whether monitoring for that form is required.
The (P) designation and dissolved form label may govern applicability of the dissolved-selenium limit and associated monitoring distinct from total recoverable selenium.

This row names a sulfate-conditioned selenium limit; whether sulfate exceeds 500 mg/l determines if this alternate limit and any related monitoring obligation apply, and whether missing selenium data should be treated as conditionally not required or unresolved.

Ce (1.5) and several aquatic/health criteria differ across columns; selecting dissolved versus total recoverable form and which column is operative changes the applicable limit and which selenium monitoring/results are in scope.

Values shown as 1E+100 may be read as a non-operative placeholder meaning no applicable numeric criterion versus a literal numeric cap; that reading changes whether a compliance comparison is possible for the affected pollutant and column.

Blank Ce with a populated Human Health Criteria value (0.47) and zero aquatic criteria creates ambiguity over whether an enforceable effluent limit exists and how to classify measurements that lack a clear Ce-based comparison basis.

Both MQL and Ce are absent while irrigation criteria show 1000 ug/l; interpretation of whether dissolved molybdenum has an enforceable effluent limit or is report-only affects limit applicability and missing-evidence handling when no Ce-based comparison is evident.
